newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. gets court order to keep Bronx plant open.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. gets court order to keep Bronx plant open.

text.p: New York state and city Friday won the first round in a battle to keep open a Bronx factory that employs 500 to 700 workers until a buyer can be found, as a judge granted a temporary restraining order.

The plant has made pots and pans under the Faberware name, and the state and city say that while there are several potential investors, they need more time to help them reach a deal. A new plant likely would make the same sorts of products, though it could not use the Faberware name, which already has been sold to another company.

A manufacturing pact between Syratech Corp, which owns the plant's capital equipment, and the firm that is responsible for its operations, US Industries, expired on Friday, and only Syratech had agreed to a 90-day extension.

"Judge Douglas McKeon granted the temporary restraining order, which means the people will report for work on Monday," said a spokesman for the Empire State Development Court, referring to the state supreme court judge.
How long the temporary restraining order will remain in place is not yet clear, as the judge, whose court is located in the Bronx, will meet with the parties on Monday.
